name: embraos-kg
description: Baseline operational knowledge about the embraOS knowledge graph itself — how memory is stored, retrieved, tagged, and curated. Distilled from docs/KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH.md; loaded at every boot so the intelligence can answer questions about its own memory without the document in the system prompt.

nodes.content: The knowledge graph is the cross-session memory: memory.entries records raw episodic turns, memory.semantic holds promoted facts, preferences, decisions, observations, and patterns, memory.procedural holds structured how-to procedures, memory.edges holds typed weighted edges between all of them, and identity.graph is the read-only projection of the sealed identity.

Promotion consolidates an episodic entry into lasting knowledge: knowledge_promote turns an entry into a semantic node with a category, or a procedural node with structured steps, stamps the entry's promoted_to pointer, and writes a derived_from provenance edge. Promotion is one-way; unlinking the node reverses it.

Edge density is the design, not bloat: every memory insert auto-derives same_session, temporal, and tag_overlap edges, and that dense structural layer is the substrate graph expansion walks. Never delete auto-derived edges to clean up — nothing re-derives them for existing documents, and read paths are ranked and windowed anyway.

Edge vocabulary: same_session, temporal, and tag_overlap are auto-derived at write time; derived_from is promotion provenance; enables, contradicts, refines, depends_on, and related_to are created deliberately via knowledge_link; free-form relation names exist only in the identity projection and in seed knowledge packs.

identity.graph nodes project the sealed identity into the knowledge graph so identity is traversable and linkable from memories. They are untouchable by the curation tools and restored on every boot; the sealed graph itself always rides the system prompt and is the source of truth.
Entries in the same session interlink automatically through same_session edges, which is how session context resurfaces in retrieval — long-running sessions build dense neighborhoods by design.

Every substantive operator message automatically retrieves the most relevant memories (the top five above a score threshold) and injects them as background context before the model call — no tool invocation needed. Very short or filler messages skip retrieval.

Retrieval collects candidates four ways — exact tag match, content-token match over memories and entries, current-session adjacency, and depth-2 graph expansion seeded from the top-scored candidates — then ranks by relevance, recency, access frequency, and confidence.
Tags are matched exactly and lowercase. A consistent, lowercase, single-word tag vocabulary — reusing established tags instead of inventing synonyms — is what keeps memories findable months later.

Every retrieval window is bounded and observable: system_status flags search_window_saturated when a memory collection outgrows the ten-thousand-document window, and traversal logs when a hub's edge window prunes.

When recorded knowledge turns out wrong, correct it in place with knowledge_update — edges and provenance survive. Reserve a contradicts edge for when both claims should stand, and knowledge_merge for true duplicates.

nodes.title: Knowledge hygiene round
nodes.description: Audit the knowledge graph, review the findings with the operator, and consolidate agreed duplicates safely.
steps: Run knowledge_audit over semantic and procedural memory
Review the dedup, orphan, rot, and contradiction findings with the operator
For each agreed duplicate pair, run knowledge_merge with dry_run=true and check the preview
Run the real merge, then re-run knowledge_audit to confirm the issues resolved

outcomes.success: Duplicates consolidated with their edges redirected; the re-audit comes back quiet.
outcomes.failure: A merge abort reports exactly what completed — re-running the same merge converges.

nodes.content: How the operator likes to work belongs in category preference, not observation. Observation is the default bucket, and preferences recorded there drown among hundreds of observations, making preference recall unreliable.
knowledge_sweep_orphans only removes edges whose endpoints no longer resolve — cleanup for dangling references after deletions, never density management.

For a preserved learning trail, patch a superseded_by field onto an outdated node with knowledge_update. It is a documented marker for readers, not a mechanism — retrieval does not down-rank nodes that carry it.

Nodes and edges loaded from seed knowledge packs are restored at boot if deleted, while edits made with knowledge_update stick. Permanently changing seeded content means revising the pack file, not deleting the node.

knowledge_query is deliberate retrieval: multi-signal ranked search with a source breakdown of direct, session, and graph hits — the way to check what the graph knows before answering from working memory alone.
knowledge_traverse walks the graph outward from any node, undirected, with edge-type and minimum-weight filters — the way to see what a memory connects to, including identity nodes.

knowledge_graph_stats reports exact node and edge counts, category and edge-type distributions, an edge provenance split (identity projection, seed packs, brain-authored), graph density, and passive orphan detection — exact at any graph size.

knowledge_audit is read-only hygiene detection: near-duplicate pairs, orphaned nodes with no meaningful edges, superseded (rot) candidates with their newer witnesses, and unacknowledged contradictions. Its dedup findings feed knowledge_merge directly.

knowledge_link records deliberate relationships — enables, contradicts, refines, depends_on, related_to — between any two nodes. These rare, meaningful edges are what make graph expansion useful, so create one whenever a real relationship is established in conversation.
knowledge_dump exports the whole graph as JSONL under /embra/workspace/KG_DUMPS for external analysis, and guardian dynamic tools can consume a dump through guardian_call's data_file bridge.

remember writes an episodic entry with tags; recall searches past entries and memories; recall with unpromoted_only=true lists the promotion backlog, newest first — the worklist for consolidating episodic memory into the graph.
forget deletes an episodic entry and cascades its edges; knowledge_unlink_node does the same for semantic and procedural nodes and clears the source entry's promotion pointer.
The DATA partition carries the entire knowledge graph and all sessions; the backup script archives STATE and DATA, so restoring DATA restores every memory.

Seed knowledge packs (*.knowledge.json) load at every boot from the OS image and from /embra/state/seed-knowledge, letting operators add baseline knowledge without conversation. This very knowledge arrived through one.
